history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration conduct a comprehensive assessment of the dependency on a single vendor for ICT contracts with a high value and assess the feasibility of adopting an exit strategy to mitigate operational risks to best protect the interest of the Organization.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Office of Information and Communications Technology conducted a comprehensive single-vendor dependency assessment covering over 10 high-value ICT contracts under the United Nations enterprise risk management framework. Assessed contracts met three objective criteria: contract duration of 10 years or longer; value at or above the Headquarters Committee on Contracts review threshold of $1.5 million; and strategic importance as enterprise- wide ICT services critical to Secretariat operations. Each contract was reviewed for single-vendor dependency risks, with mitigation measures and risk treatment plans documented. Vendor lock-in and dependency risks are actively mitigated via technical diversification (e.g., VMware-to- Proxmox migration), enhanced contractual exit/transition clauses and regular market scanning for alternative suppliers. Clear exit strategies and contingency pathways with execution triggers and transition timelines are in place for all critical ICT vendors. Detailed contract-level analysis, mitigation actions and risk ownership are compiled in the vendor- dependency risk register. The Office of Information and Communications Technology will maintain annual updates and reviews ahead of major contract renewals to align with operational risks and market changes.
history.board_assessment: Given that a comprehensive assessment of single-vendor dependency across more than 10 high-value ICT contracts has been completed and corresponding mitigation measures and risk-treatment plans have been documented for each contract, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
